storage: Project definitions are files under projects/<project-id>. SQLite is a rebuildable index plus local approval and run state. Never edit SQLite.
draftArtifacts: For a structured draft preview in run History, write an artifact ending in .draft.json: {"schema":"inferay.draft/1","draft":{"title":"Draft title","text":"Literal draft text","details":[{"label":"Channel","value":"Instagram"}]}}. Details are optional. The preview does not publish anything. Use Markdown artifacts for formatted reports.
references: Repository references use UUIDs with local checkout bindings. Local skill references use UUIDs; global skills use global:<id>. Direct tool executions use a local tool folder name. Agent executions optionally declare tools: [{pluginId: PLUGIN_UUID, toolId: TOOL_UUID}]. These grants expose inferay_tools list/call for both providers; every referenced library is pinned by approval. Library permissions must fit within the automation permissions.
approval: createPlugin, updatePlugin and automation saveDefinition prepare validated proposal cards without saving or enabling anything. The user saves from the card. Execution requires separate approval tied to the exact input hash. Edits revoke approvals and disable schedules. Never claim a proposal is saved or active.
writeRules: expectedHash=null creates a new file only; updating requires the current sourceHash. Keep UUIDs stable. A successful save changes the file and rebuilds its index; it does not approve execution.

execution.instructions: Review the selected resources and summarize changes with evidence.

bundleRules: Use createPlugin for a reusable library, including its manifest, README and needed code, assets or local skills in one files map. Tools and automations are optional; do not invent a schedule for a code library. Group related helpers and jobs by purpose rather than creating one plugin per automation. Paths are relative to plugins/<slug>. Existing plugin folders cannot be replaced by createPlugin. Reuse existing global skills using global:<id> instead of creating copies. Every JSON file is a serialized string. Match the plugin may list to the automation permissions. Saving installs the bundle with schedules off. Update an existing library with updatePlugin using its whole-library sourceHash from readPlugin. Supply complete text only for added or replaced files, and explicit relative file paths in remove. Unmentioned files, including binary assets, are preserved. Keep the manifest UUID unchanged. Updates are validated as one complete package, shown in one proposal card, and published atomically when accepted. Never call createPlugin to replace an existing library.
plugins: A plugin is a persistent workspace for reusable capabilities: code, helper modules, documentation, templates and supporting assets. Skills teach when and how to use it; automations optionally schedule work using it. Neither skills nor automations are required. Discover existing plugins before building another implementation. Put a concise usage guide in README.md and describe the capability in plugin.json. Declare tool entry points when Inferay must execute a script. Keep project knowledge in Memory and generated results in run artifacts; never bundle credentials.
readRules: List projects to discover plugin names and descriptions. readPlugin with path=null lists the library files and hashes; supply a relative path such as README.md or src/render.py to read UTF-8 content. Reading never executes code or approves it. Inspect the usage guide before reuse.
automationRules: For a standalone job, use saveDefinition at automations/<id>/automation.json. This previews and validates an automation proposal card; it never writes from the agent call. Use the current sourceHash from list when proposing an update, and null only for a new file. Preserve the automation UUID. Reuse global skills; do not create a plugin or companion skill for an ordinary automation request. Use calendar triggers with an explicit local time and timezone for daily or weekly schedules.
toolRules: Project automations may select library skills as plugin:<plugin UUID>:<skill UUID>; bare skill UUIDs refer to the automation owner, and global:<id> selects a global skill. Agent tool grants may include required:true to require a successful latest call before the run can succeed; use this for quality checks and mandatory outputs. Tools live under tools/<slug>/tool.json with program, entrypoint, args, timeoutSeconds, inputSchema and outputSchema. Default interface=json_stdin passes JSON on stdin and requires JSON stdout. For an ordinary script use interface=cli and args with exactly one {entrypoint} token plus optional {input.field} whole-argument tokens. Inputs must be strings, numbers or booleans; no shell interpolation occurs. Example Python args: ["{entrypoint}","--caption","{input.caption}"]. Blender args: ["--background","--python","{entrypoint}","--","{input.scene}"]. CLI exit zero yields {stdout,stderr,exitCode:0}, validated by outputSchema; nonzero fails the run. Use {output} or {output}/relative-path for a run-specific output directory or file prefix; input strings are never re-expanded. Successful CLI output files are automatically registered as artifacts (at most 100, under 50 MB each); symlinks and special files fail collection. Both streams are logged. For a local stdio MCP server use interface={"mcp":{"tool":"DECLARED_TOOL_NAME"}} with program, entrypoint and literal args. Inferay initializes the server, discovers that tool and calls it with the input. It returns {response:MCP_RESULT,artifacts:[relative paths]}, checked against outputSchema, and reserves mcp-response.json for the retained response. This uses the same approval, process permissions, timeouts and agent grants as other tools; do not add a second server execution path or inherit ambient provider MCP settings. A missing tool, protocol failure or MCP isError fails the call. Authenticated remote MCP connections are not supported yet. Rendering tools on Apple Silicon must declare gpu in both the library and automation may lists; this grants Metal device/context/compiler services without network or extra writable roots. Local tools require the macOS sandbox; other platforms currently refuse them. Optional requires on plugin.json or tool.json declares programs, minimum versions or Python modules, for example [blender>=5.0, ffmpeg, python3:numpy]. A repository-backed tool adds pack: {repositoryId: UUID, commit: FULL_GIT_COMMIT, sha256: ENTRYPOINT_SHA256}; entrypoint and cwd then refer to the linked checkout root. Its clean checkout must match the pins; untracked/ignored files, sparse or assume-unchanged entries, submodules and escaping or invalid symlinks are refused; tracked aliases inside the checkout are allowed. Never copy the kit merely to avoid a missing binding or pin: ask to link a clean checkout. Missing requirements and mismatched pins block execution.
connectionRules: Never store credentials in library files, tool inputs or instructions. A tool may declare connections: {SERVICE: {id: LOCAL_CONNECTION_UUID, baseUrl: HTTPS_URL_ENDING_IN_SLASH, header: Authorization, prefix: "Bearer "}}. The user manages keys in Plugins → Connections; do not invent IDs. With approved network permission the tool receives INFERAY_CONNECTIONS_URL. GET that URL plus /SERVICE?path=<URL-encoded relative path>; Inferay attaches the key only to the approved destination. No raw key enters the tool. Requests are GET-only, limited to 64 per invocation, 30 seconds and 1 MiB each; redirects and credential echoes are rejected. Access expires when the tool ends. This does not implement publication or authenticated remote MCP.
